name: QuizWhizzer

Pricing (company-stated): free forever, Pro $39 a year. Founded Oct 2019, UK. Listed for sale at $30,000, about 1.6× (TrustMRR). L30 profit margin 40% (TrustMRR snapshot).

mentions.indieAngle: Ship a simple teacher tool, ride search for a decade, sell when you are bored. An annual Pro keeps renewals calm.

whyItPrints: A classroom quiz tool that kept collecting annual Pro plans without a growth team. Maintenance mode plus search traffic is the quiet exit.
whyThisMatters:
QuizWhizzer turns a classroom review into a race. The teacher hosts, students join with a username and no account, and up to about a hundred people can play. There is no app to install. Question types include multiple choice, true or false, ordering, short text, and audio. Power-ups and a shared board are the game layer. A quiz can be generated from a topic, with an explanation on each question. Students' names are just a username.

The company is in the UK and was founded in 2019. The founder says it has mostly sat in maintenance mode and still gets a few hundred organic signups a day. The site puts the teacher count above 450,000. Pricing on the listing is a free tier and a yearly Pro. The homepage now shows a free tier and a higher yearly price than the listing recorded, so the two figures should not be collapsed into one. The product is for sale. The last year of Stripe cash is modest next to the all-time total, which fits a long-running annual plan that is no longer being pushed.

You pay once a year so the review session is a game instead of a worksheet.
